verified.headline: Brazil trims GDP outlook, sees slower recovery amid cautious monetary easing cycle

publication.evidence: WTAQ displayed September 22 at 12:34 p.m.; editorial qualification treated the local display as CDT (UTC−05:00), yielding 17:34Z.

verified.evidence: Full Reuters report read. It gives the Finance Ministry's revisions to 2026 GDP growth (2.3% to 2.0%) and 2027 (2.5% to 2.3%), a 2.6% average growth projection for 2028–2030, and inflation forecasts of 4.9% for 2026 (from 5.1%) and 3.8% for 2027 (from 3.6%). The ministry attributed weaker services/industry and a gradual easing path in its baseline; all are projections. Reuters separately reports market consensus below the official growth forecasts.

facts: Reuters reports 2026 GDP growth forecast cut from 2.3% to 2.0%, 2027 from 2.5% to 2.3%, and inflation from 5.1% to 4.9%.
qualifications: The WTAQ display was treated as CDT for UTC conversion; macro figures are government projections, not outcomes.

verified.selectionReason: Selected for a timely and independently reported revision to the government's macroeconomic baseline, with official Ministry confirmation. The story separates official projections from surveyed market expectations and attributes explanations rather than treating forecast changes as outcomes.

corroboratingSources.matchingFacts: The Ministry of Finance's September projection page confirms the revisions and forecast figures.

verified.corroborationNote: Official Ministry figures corroborate the projections; the reported market-survey values remain attributed to Reuters.

extractionGates.bodyContaminationNote: Full source body reviewed; selection qualification found no caption, recommendation or sidebar contamination.

reviewFlags: All macroeconomic figures are identified as official forecasts for stated years, not outcomes; market estimates are attributed to Reuters.
